column1: # Per-module elaboration parameters for CORE-ET tops.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  A PARAMETERIZED module has no single semantics: it
# denotes a family, one member per parameter assignment.  Elaborating such a
# module as a TOP therefore needs the parameters supplied from outside, and the
# certificate that results is a certificate for THAT MEMBER -- never for the
# family.  Recording the assignment here is what makes the claim checkable
# instead of implicit in someone's command line.
# `txfma_adder` declares `parameter int unsigned Width = 0` and is correct when
# INSTANTIATED; standalone it elaborates to `logic [-1:0]` ports and slang
# refuses it, which is the whole of its "compile-failed" census row.
# Width 10 is `TXFMA_EXP_SEXT_PS_SZ` (vpu_defs_pkg.sv:855).  It is the most
# common instantiation by a wide margin but NOT the only one -- an earlier note
# here said "10 of 10", which was the right numerator against the wrong
# denominator.  Measured over every `txfma_adder` instantiation in core-et's
# RTL (16 sites; two more in testbenches pass their own parameter through):
#   Width expression          value  sites  where
#   TXFMA_EXP_SEXT_PS_SZ         10     10  txfma_e1:165,198,213,229,245
#   TXFMA_ETRZ_PROD_PS_SZ         6      1  txfma_e1:278
#   TXFMA_ETRZ_PROD_PH_SZ         5      1  txfma_e1:261
#   TXFMA_EXP_PS_SZ         FLOAT32_E     1  txfma_e6:76
#   TXFMA_A3+1                   64      1  txfma_f2:124
#   TXFMA_A3-TXFMA_B47+1         52      1  txfma_f4:72
#   rnd_adder_width          (local)      1  txfma_rnd_adder:50
# So this certificate covers the 10-bit member, which 10 of the 16 RTL
# instantiations use.  The other six widths are NOT covered by it, and a
# certificate for a different member would need its own row.
# The flags go to BOTH elaborations: the implementation read AND the LEC
# reference read.  Giving only one of them the parameters would have the two
# sides elaborate different designs, and the LEC would compare a 10-bit adder
# against a degenerate one -- a mismatch with nothing wrong in the tool.
# module<TAB>slang_flags<TAB>why
txfma_adder
column3: parameterized leaf; Width 10 = TXFMA_EXP_SEXT_PS_SZ, used by 10 of 10 in-tree instantiations
